judged_text: The diff adds three behavior-bearing modules — parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens, and the app-credential webhook endpoint — with no test anywhere in the diff exercising any of them. The exact defect class this diff ships (the safeParse envelope persisted as a credential key in GoogleCalendarService, the '[object Object]' computed schema keys, the literal refresh_token placeholder) would be caught by one unit test asserting the persisted key shape or the parsed output, so the next refactor of this path regresses the same way; a regression here breaks OAuth refresh for seven integrations at once.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces verifiable correctness defects, not just “missing tests”. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()`; `z.string()` is an object and `.toString()` will not produce a meaningful dynamic key (likely `"[object Object]"`), so the schema does not do what the comments intend. Also `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *safeParse result object* (with `.success`/`.data`), and in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the returned value is directly persisted as `key` (`const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`), meaning the credential key will be the safeParse envelope rather than the decrypted credential shape. These are concrete, diff-grounded defects that can break OAuth refresh behavior.
